record.issuing_body: Ministers and high-level authorities of Latin American and Caribbean countries at the Second Ministerial and High-Level Authorities Summit on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, Montevideo (organised by Uruguay's AGESIC with UNESCO and CAF)
record.notes: Follow-up to the Santiago Declaration of October 2023 (INT-12), in line with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI; it also highlights the UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology and CAF's practical guide on designing AI public policies. The declaration and its roadmap were approved at the summit's closed session on 4 October 2024 with representatives of Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Curaçao, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, the Dominican Republic and Uruguay; Bolivia and Dominica adhered later (update as of 1 December 2024), and Antigua and Barbuda (update as of 1 September 2025). The roadmap (version of 2 October 2024) calls for clear responsibilities among actors in the AI ecosystem and plans a methodology for designing AI regulatory proposals, annual reports on the use of UNESCO's readiness and ethical impact assessment tools, a regional study on racism and discrimination in AI used for public security, and guidelines on data governance for algorithm training, over a 12-month horizon with half-yearly follow-up. Chile handed leadership of the Working Group to Uruguay. The third summit, held in Santo Domingo on 25-26 June 2026, approved the Declaration of Santo Domingo and a 2026-2027 roadmap.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the English and Spanish declaration PDFs ('version 4.0'), the English roadmap PDF, the AGESIC news item of 4 October 2024 and the AGESIC news item of 20 July 2026 on the third summit, all on gub.uy. The declaration PDFs confirm the title, the Spanish title, the summit dates, the resolutions, approval at the closed session of 4 October 2024, the countries present and the later adhesions; the roadmap gives the five areas and their products; the 2024 news item confirms the approval, the working-group hand-over and the next host; the 2026 news item reports the Santo Domingo summit and its declaration.

record.original_title: Declaración de Montevideo: Para la construcción de un enfoque regional sobre la gobernanza de la Inteligencia Artificial y sus impactos en nuestra sociedad
record.summary: Ministerial declaration adopted at the second regional summit on AI ethics (Montevideo, 3-4 October 2024) that reaffirms human-rights-centred AI governance, promotes international cooperation to maximise AI's benefits and mitigate its risks, and approves the Roadmap for Ethical AI for Latin America and the Caribbean 2024-2025. The roadmap's five areas are governance and regulation (including a mechanism against AI-amplified disinformation), talent and the future of work, protection of vulnerable groups, environment and climate change, and infrastructure. The declaration consolidates the regional Working Group on AI Ethics as a permanent dialogue body and makes the ministerial summit annual.

judgment.status_reasoning: A ministerial declaration approved on 4 October 2024 and still gathering adhesions (Antigua and Barbuda, update as of 1 September 2025). Its 2024-2025 roadmap had a 12-month horizon, and the third summit approved a new 2026-2027 roadmap and the Declaration of Santo Domingo in June 2026; the stored sources say the new texts build on the Montevideo summit, not that they replace the declaration. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.date_reasoning: The footnote gives approval at the closed session held on 4 October 2024; the summit ran on 3 and 4 October 2024.
